Music Flat Sign Symbol

There is no legacy Windows Alt code for Music Flat Sign because it is not in either the OEM code page 437 or Windows-1252 tables. The Unicode codepoint is U+266D, which you can use as ♭ in HTML, \266D in CSS, or type with Alt+9837 on Windows (BMP only). If your keyboard has no numeric keypad, use the Character Viewer, the HTML entity, or copy the character directly. Music Flat Sign is outside both legacy code pages, which is why U+266D is the identifier that works across Word, HTML, CSS, Python and JavaScript. Music Flat Sign has no named HTML entity, so use the numeric escape ♭ or the hex escape ♭.

How to type music flat sign on Windows

  1. Turn Num Lock on so the numeric keypad is active.
  2. Hold the left Alt key.
  3. Type 9 8 3 7 on the numeric keypad for the decimal codepoint 9837.
  4. Release Alt. The Music Flat Sign character (♭) appears.

If your keyboard has no numeric keypad, see how to type symbols without a numpad.

How to type music flat sign on macOS

There is no direct Option shortcut for Music Flat Sign. Open the Character Viewer with ⌃⌘Space, search for "Music Flat Sign" and click the character to insert it.

How to use music flat sign in code

  • HTML: or
  • CSS: content:"\266D"; ()
  • Python: \u266D or chr(0x266D)
  • JavaScript: \u266D or String.fromCodePoint(0x266D)
  • JSON: "\u266D"

Frequently asked questions

Is there an Alt code for ♭?

No legacy Alt code exists for Music Flat Sign because it is not in code page 437 or Windows-1252. Use the Unicode codepoint U+266D in HTML, CSS or the Character Viewer instead.

How do I type ♭ without a numpad?

Use the Windows Character Viewer (Win+.), the macOS Character Viewer (⌃⌘Space), an HTML entity such as ♭, or copy the character directly from this page.

Why does Alt+9837 not work?

Alt+9837 only works on a keyboard with a physical numeric keypad. It also requires the application to accept the numeric-keypad input path. Laptops without a numpad need an alternative method.

What is the Unicode for Music Flat Sign?

The Unicode codepoint for Music Flat Sign is U+266D. You can use this value in HTML as ♭, in CSS as \266D, and in Word with Alt+X.

How do I type ♭ on a Mac?

Open the Character Viewer with ⌃⌘Space and search for the character name or U+266D, then click it.
